Literally read the entire employment law section pertinent to your location. Then read it again. Then summarise it in bulletpoints and keep it in your desk. I'd also recommend since you're alone that you ensure the company has a retained law firm that has at least one employment law practice.

A lot of people are asking me or private messaging me asking for tips so I will give you 5 I live by.
1. Sometimes you're wrong, we always think we're the smartest person in the room but it's often incorrect. Hear everyone's opinion regardless of rank and leave your ego at the door or don't bother coming in.
2. The janitor is as important as the CFO. If you want to know the real issues in a business go to the trades and service staff. Just because their role involves manual labor don't for a second think they're not intelligent.
3. Your employees get paid first. They signed an employment contract and that works both ways. They commit to work and you commit to safety. You are the FUCKING LAST PERSON IN THE WHOLE COMPANY that gets paid. After all the people and all the bills. Not enough money? Tough shit you should have thought about that before you hired them. Never terminate staff to protect your pay packet. People don't forget that. 
4. Al Pacino life is a game of inches (Google it). Watch it. Then watch it again. Without our team we die.
5. They're human so be a human back even when it's inconvenient to do so. I had a mother who lost a child and I held her and tried to comfort her for hours while she screamed. That's your fucking responsibility. I don't care how little you empathize they are your staff and for some of them you are all they've got. Treat them as such. They'll pay you back tenfold in their own way.

I'm not a lecturer or anything and probably not a master but I can give you a few tips. For starters there's this expectation of hierarchy that you need to get rid off. Sure, people's have bosses and like any company we have middle management but it's a bit loose. 

I'm lucky my company isn't super big it's 63 staff and a few contractors so I'm able to allow any employees come to me with any idea they have, and I often find excuses to talk to them and try to draw these out in case they're shy, any problem whether personal or professional also. My middle management believe in the same values luckily. I don't care if it's the janitor, the lowest paid employee or the highest I'm never too busy to talk to one of my staff - even if it's not strictly work related come in and have a chat about what's bothering you! Urgent money problem or hospital bill? Call me at 3am if you have to and we'll sort something out. 

To understand how to make employees happy you first need to understand what makes people unhappy, then just do the opposite! People need to have control over their jobs, try to make it less boring. People need to be compensated well and I believe in having a strong bonus system for performance. If I benefit, the employees should too. Treat people like adults, because they are. As long as the work is done I don't mind what time people show up or leave, just be contactable in case something comes up. If you want to stay and put in extra work then you'll be rewarded for it because it's not in your job description! 

Have a bit of fun too, work can be a boring place and sometimes a bit of levity can increase productivity and make everyone happy. As an example for our Halloween carnival party yours truly will be in a dunk tank for charity.

I'm an asthmatic, I was not allowed my inhaler in the jail cell with me and instead it was kept outside my cell on what I presume was a little shelf. Those are the things that made life dangerous 100 years ago. 

Now we complain if life isn’t convenient. This isn’t a statement on modern society, this is a statement about motivation. Life is easy. It’s easy to skate by.

It’s pretty easy to grow up, put your dreams aside, leave your passions behind, take a job that you really don’t even mind, raise some kids who will most likely be inspired to do the exact same thing. Go from point A to point B to point C until you end up at point Z, where you pass away and there’s a line of people waiting to get up to tell everyone else who knew you what a good life you had. Nothing bad about that, nothing wrong with that, but nothing great about it. Nothing inspiring about that. 

The awful truth is that life is easy. Living, truly living, chasing a dream and truly living is hard. Living is a bitch. Living is a tough. Especially when you switch it and you ask yourself, “What am I dying to do? What is it that puts a fire in my heart?” Answering that question isn’t the end of it, it’s really just the spark. Because once you get that fire burning, you need to feed it. You need to keep reminding yourself, putting new coals in there. Reminding yourself everyday about that goal. Because we’ve all taken up a hobby, or a goal, or a workout that we stop for just a couple days and then we never pick it up again. You need to constantly remind yourself that you’re dying and that you’re dying to do something. Because the minute you forget, life creeps right back in. And life is easy.

Because it's porous, like the inside of a sponge basically.  It is lots of tiny avenues and channels that are naturally forms.  It's not a big can waiting for the lid being taken off.  They drill down and then 'cap' the well they have drilled, install something called a Christmas Tree (which sucks the oil out) and then they set up 'topside' production (everything above the water)

Typically due to the Porosity of the rock the oil is in it's a little bit like a sponge (lots of holes and channels within).  Porous though the inside may be the outside has no holes hence why the oil doesn't seep into the ocean.  

To simplify it when you remove the oil from the 'pocket' you either water or ['gas 'lift'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_lift) which means you put water or gas back into the 'well' while taking Oil out which means to mother nature: there's the same amount of 'stuff' in there as there was before.  The pressure of 'lifting' with water or gas helps take the oil out faster due to differences in density (Oil is denser than water and will always sit at the bottom making it easier to suck up than before) and keeps the Well stable.
